cover.title: Never take his picture without asking

lines.text: This doll gets letters every year... from people begging him to forgive them.
Key West, Florida. Early nineteen hundreds. A little boy named Gene Otto is given a doll almost as big as he is.
Gene names the doll Robert. His own first name. He even dresses it in his own sailor suit.
When things went wrong in the house, Gene always had the same answer. Robert did it.
Gene grew up to be an artist. He kept Robert his whole life, in the house on Eaton Street.
Gene died in 1974. The next owner of the house claimed the doll moved on its own... and that she heard footsteps in the attic.
In 1994, Robert was donated to the Fort East Martello Museum.
Today he sits behind glass, holding a toy lion. Visitors are told one rule: ask his permission before you take his picture.
People who didn't ask blame him for car wrecks, breakups, lost jobs. And the museum keeps getting letters, apologizing to Robert.
Would you ask him first? Comment sorry Robert... just in case. Sleep tight, partner.
